Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — expected traffic and context needs

Hi Soojin — thanks again for the demo last week. A couple of data points from our side to shape the model recommendations: 

- Primary use case: automated clinical note summarization + structured diagnosis extraction for telehealth visits.
- Concurrent users at launch: ~120 peak (US east region). Expected steady daily active users ~3k.
- Average session length (turns): 6 user turns, ~1.2k input tokens per session (most of that is clinic notes).
- 95th percentile context requirement: ~6k tokens when including patient history + encounter notes.
- Latency SLA target: P95 generation end-to-end <500ms for short answers, <1.2s for structured extraction.
- Monthly tokens (estimate): ~450M input tokens, ~150M output tokens.

We also have a procurement review next week; cc'd procurement to loop them in. Can you share a short model shortlist and any immediate sizing guidance so our infra team can prep?

Thanks — Sam
Sam Kelly
Head of Product, ClariHealth
sam.kelly@clarihealth.ai

Hi Sam — great details, this is exactly what we needed. High level response below and we will follow up with a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a one-page sizing sheet. Attaching a quick token profile export for your numbers.

Key recommendations (summary):
- Shortlist candidates: Redwood-open-7B-quant (4k/8k variant), Mistral-8k-eye (8k native), and Redwood-32k-ctx (if you want headroom for growth).
- Context path: for 6k P95 we recommend testing the Redwood-32k-ctx variant in a canary because it preserves long-form KV cache and avoids chunking. If latency under that config is above target, fallback policy to Mistral-8k-eye with prefix caching is viable.
- Throughput sizing (initial): for 120 concurrent peak users and your token mix, estimate sustained token generation rate ~12k tokens/s across the fleet during peak. That maps to ~8–10 GPUs in dedicated pool with mixed batching; exact count depends on quantization and seq-length distribution.
- Cost levers: enable prefix/KV caching for clinical templates, aggressive prefix caching of static history, and 8-bit quantized weights for inference to reduce GPU TFLOPS needs.

Next steps: Monica will own the benchmark sprint with your infra; Grace will provide the detailed shortlist + perf notes; I will share the MAP and scheduling options for a canary window.

Attachments: ClariHealth_token_profile.csv

—
Soojin Lee

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: candidate models + initial perf expectations for ClariHealth

Soojin / Monica / Vivek — I took Sam's numbers and sketched a shortlist and an initial perf matrix. See notes below and I attached an editable shortlist workbook. This is internal until we finalize.

Model shortlist rationale:
- Redwood-open-7B-quant (8k variant) — low-cost baseline, good for extraction tasks with tuned prompts; expected P95 generation (~0.6–0.9s) for typical 1k tokens outputs when quantized and with prefix cache.
- Mistral-8k-eye — strong quality on long-context summarization and moderately sized; expected to hit ~0.8–1.1s at 6k context when running on A100/MI300 class with tuned batching.
- Redwood-32k-ctx (float16/8-bit combo) — for 6k+ context it's the safest for correctness; latency tradeoff but reduces chunking artifacts. Expect P95 ~1.0–1.4s depending on kernel selection.
- Fallback: gpt-4o-mini (partner model) — higher latency/cost but useful for hard-extraction edge cases; keep as late-step fallback in route policy.

Sizing assumptions used in workbook:
- Peak concurrency: 120 active sessions; we assume 6 requests/session and avg 1.2k input tokens per session.
- Batch sizing: dynamic batching target 32–48 depending on latency window.
- Cache hit assumptions: 30% prefix cache hit for reuseable clinical templates, 10% KV reuse across multi-turn sessions.

Immediate asks for Monica (benchmarks):
1) Run end-to-end perf tests for the three shortlist candidates using the token profile attached. Prioritize Redwood-32k-ctx and Mistral-8k-eye.
2) Provide GPU SKU mapping and a minimal dedicated pool suggestion (min/target/burst).
3) Produce a short 1-slide perf vs cost comparison for the customer deck.

I'll sync with Vivek on rollout policy (canary windows + automated fallback) after Monica posts results.

Attachment: ClariHealth_model_shortlist.xlsx

—
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Sam / team — attaching the MAP and a concise committed-capacity sketch. Highlights and action owners below. Full MAP attached as PDF.

Summary (short):
- Commit suggestion (initial): 10 dedicated GPUs (mix of 4 x L40s + 6 x A100s) to meet your P95 goals with the Redwood-32k-ctx canary + Mistral-8k-eye fallback. Burst policy: auto-burst to Redwood hosted pool up to 30% additional capacity; automatic fallback to quantized 7B variant if both pools constrained.
- Client changes: prefix/KV caching requires adding a small metadata header to requests (we provided a lightweight adapter in the MAP). No full pipeline rewrite needed; infra estimated effort: ~1–2 engineer-days.

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
1) This week: Monica runs perf sprint (Monica). Deliverables: perf report + GPU SKU map (2 business days).
2) Next week: Canary window (Soojin/ClariHealth infra) — 72-hour canary on Redwood-32k-ctx with production trace sampling.
3) Procurement kickoff: finalize committed GPU count and contract terms (Procurement + Soojin).
4) Go-live: scale to committed pool, enable KV-prefix caching, monitor quality regressions and cost delta (Grace/Vivek).

Attachments: MAP-ClariHealth-v1.pdf, ClariHealth_model_shortlist.xlsx, ClariHealth_token_profile.csv
